description: Correlix / NetOps_Observability dependency-patch automation (see
NetOps_Observability/docs/design/PATCH_AUTOMATION_PLAN_2026-09-03.md for the
reasoning and NetOps_Observability/docs/runbooks/patch-train.md for the
monthly procedure).
WHY RENOVATE AND NOT DEPENDABOT: Dependabot's `docker` ecosystem reads
Dockerfiles ONLY -- it cannot see the 27 `image:` pins in
deployment/docker/docker-compose.yml, which is where most of this product's
third-party attack surface actually lives. It also has no way to track a
version that is written as a plain string (GO_VERSION, STATICCHECK_VERSION,
GOSEC_VERSION, GOVULNCHECK_VERSION, GOLANGCI_VERSION, GITLEAKS_VERSION,
RUFF_VERSION, ...), and no native automerge. All three are load-bearing here,
so this config replaces .github/dependabot.yml. GitHub's Dependabot ALERTS
(the repo setting) stay ON -- `vulnerabilityAlerts` below consumes them.
ZERO TRUST (CLAUDE.md 3): this is intended to run SELF-HOSTED from
.github/workflows/renovate.yml, not via the third-party Mend Renovate App. No
external service gets write access to the repository.
CLAUDE.md 6 IS NOT NEGOTIABLE BY A BOT: Renovate can only bump modules that
are already in go.mod -- it can never ADD one. Majors of the allowlisted
modules are dependencyDashboardApproval-gated and never automerged, because a
major is a re-review of the allowlist entry, not a patch.
enabledManagers is an ALLOWLIST: a manager we did not ask for cannot open a PR against a file class nobody reviews.
constraints pins Go resolution to the toolchain the module actually declares (go.mod: go 1.26.0 / toolchain go1.26.8).

gomod.description: vendor/ is committed and `GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor GOPROXY=off go build ./...` is a REQUIRED check. Renovate re-runs `go mod vendor` itself when it sees vendor/modules.txt; the offline-build check is the backstop that fails the PR if the vendor tree ever comes back stale.

npm.description: package.json uses caret ranges; `bump` keeps the manifest and the lockfile telling the same story so a reviewer can read the diff.

pip-compile.description: src/correlation/requirements.txt is hash-locked (SC-011) and generated by `pip-compile --generate-hashes --output-file=requirements.txt requirements.in`. Renovate re-runs that command, so the --require-hashes lock stays valid. The plain pip_requirements manager MUST stay off for this path (it would rewrite pins and orphan the hashes).

github-actions.description: SC-002: every `uses:` stays SHA-pinned with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment. pinDigests keeps new entries honest too.

customManagers.description: Go GATE TOOLS pinned as workflow env vars in backend-ci.yml. Each is installed with `go install <module>@<version>`, so the `go` datasource resolves exactly what CI will fetch. One manager PER TOOL: a regex manager binds one depName, so a shared block would mislabel every match.
GOLANGCI_VERSION is duplicated in scripts/ci-backend-guard.sh (the local mirror of the CI gate). Both files are matched so the pin can never split.
Go TOOLCHAIN as a workflow env var. go.mod's `go`/`toolchain` directives are handled natively by the gomod manager; this catches the CI half so they move together.
gitleaks is downloaded by tag in supply-chain.yml (SC-007/SC-010).

Python gate tools pinned as workflow env vars in correlation-ci.yml -- one manager per tool, same reason as the Go set. NEVER automerged: an unpinned ruff bump turned a green branch red on 2026-07-25 with no Python changed, which is why these are pinned at all.
pytest is pinned in THREE workflows on purpose and they are deliberately NOT aligned (see the note in correlation-ci.yml). Each is tracked separately so a bump is an explicit decision per lane.

packageRules.description: DEFAULT: nothing automerges. Every rule below that turns it on is an explicit, reasoned exception.

1. GO TOOLCHAIN TRAIN. go.mod `go`/`toolchain`, the CI GO_VERSION, and the golang:*-alpine builder digest in the Dockerfiles are ONE change or they are a broken build (a scanner binary built with an older Go refuses to load a newer module -- backend-ci.yml documents exactly this). Grouped, never automerged: raising the toolchain is the playbook in docs/runbooks/patch-train.md, not a robot's call.
prBodyNotes: :warning: **Toolchain raise.** Follow `NetOps_Observability/docs/runbooks/patch-train.md` -> *Toolchain raise playbook*. This PR is incomplete until go.mod (`go`/`toolchain`), `GO_VERSION`, the `golang:*-alpine` FROM digests in `Dockerfile.backend`, `mock-nms/Dockerfile`, `mock-servicenow/Dockerfile`, and the four gate-tool pins all move together AND the offline-build check is green.

packageRules.description: The golang builder base image is part of the same train.

2. GO GATE TOOLS (CLAUDE.md 8/12). Grouped so staticcheck/gosec/govulncheck/golangci-lint move as one set. NEVER automerged: a new linter release can fail a branch that changed no code, and the fix belongs in the same commit as the bump.
prBodyNotes: Gate-tool bump. Expect NEW findings: fix them in THIS PR, do not merge a bump that needs a follow-up. `GOLANGCI_VERSION` also lives in `NetOps_Observability/scripts/ci-backend-guard.sh` -- both are updated by this PR; verify.

packageRules.description: 3. PYTHON GATE TOOLS. Same lesson, learned the hard way on 2026-07-25 (ruff 0.16: 250 findings between two commits that touched no Python).
prBodyNotes: Linter/test-runner bump. Fix whatever the new rules find IN THIS PR (see the `env:` comment in `correlation-ci.yml`).

packageRules.description: 4. GO MODULES -- the CLAUDE.md 6 allowlist. Patch/minor may automerge on a fully green gate (which includes govulncheck, -race, the pg-integration RLS suite, and the offline vendor build).

MAJORS of an allowlisted module are an allowlist RE-REVIEW (CLAUDE.md 6 gates: need / offline / pinned / minimal surface). No PR opens without a human ticking it on the dashboard, and it can never automerge.
prBodyNotes: :stop_sign: **CLAUDE.md 6 allowlist re-review required.** A major is not a patch: re-run all four gates (need / offline-buildable / pinned & reviewed / minimal surface) and update the allowlist table's Notes column in `CLAUDE.md` in this PR.

packageRules.description: The three stdlib-only satellite modules (mock-nms, mock-servicenow, installer-gui) have no requires -- only a `go` directive. Renovate should keep their directive in step with the backend, but never automerge it (see the go toolchain group).

5. CONTAINER IMAGES -- digest-only refresh (same tag, upstream rebuilt). This is the single highest-value automation in the repo: it is how a rebuilt base image carrying a distro CVE fix actually reaches the 27 compose pins without a human retyping a sha256.
A TAG change (postgres 16 -> 17, opensearch 2.16 -> 2.17, kafka 4.1 -> 4.2) moves a stateful service and can require a data migration. Human only.
prBodyNotes: Image **tag** change, not a digest refresh. Check `NetOps_Observability/docs/UPGRADE.md` and `docs/runbooks/upgrade-bootstraps.md` before merging: postgres / opensearch / clickhouse / kafka carry on-disk state.

packageRules.description: Stateful data stores get an extra hold: never automerge, never grouped with the rest.
6. GITHUB ACTIONS (SC-002). Digest bumps behind an unchanged tag automerge; a version bump is reviewed.

7. FRONTEND npm. Dev deps automerge on patch/minor (the blocking gate is `tsc -b && vite build` + vitest + Playwright E2E, which is a real signal). Runtime deps automerge on patch only -- the dashboard is the product surface.
Playwright's npm package and its downloaded browser build must match; the pin is exact on purpose. Never automerge.
prBodyNotes: `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium` in frontend-ci.yml must resolve the matching browser build. Verify the E2E job is green, not just the type-check.

packageRules.description: 8. DOCS PORTAL npm. Docusaurus 3.5.2 is pinned exact and its build chain is Node 18 (see the GHSA-5c6j-r48x-rmvq entry in .trivyignore.yaml). Grouped, never automerged, low priority -- it ships no product runtime code.
9. CORRELATION runtime (hash-locked). Patch automerges; anything larger touches the engine that consumes the bus.
10. LAB-ONLY trees are not shipped (make-installer.sh LAB_PATHS). Tracked on the dashboard, but they never open a PR on their own and never block the train.
11. Give every dependency a settling period. A release yanked six hours after publication must never have reached main. Security PRs bypass this via vulnerabilityAlerts below.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: IMMEDIATE lane. A published advisory does not wait for Monday. Still never automerged: the emergency path in docs/runbooks/patch-train.md requires a human to run the gate, rebuild from a clean checkout, and deploy-qualify.
prBodyNotes: :rotating_light: **Security advisory.** Follow `NetOps_Observability/docs/runbooks/patch-train.md` -> *Emergency path (CVE in a running lane)*: bump -> full gate -> rebuild from a CLEAN checkout -> `scripts/deploy-qualify.sh` (bootstraps + engines-actually-consuming proof). `docker compose up` exiting 0 is not evidence of anything.
